findings.export: The command documentation includes /mergedpolicy for merging domain and local policy, /areas securitypolicy for the security-policy area, and a required /cfg output path. This defines command syntax, not which PasswordComplexity values are returned or whether an export is an effective-policy read.
findings.generateRollback: The command requires /db, /cfg and /rbk paths; Microsoft warns a repeated run overwrites an existing rollback template and documents mismatch logging to scesrv.log.
findings.configure: The command applies security settings from its database to the current system and is state-changing.
findings.import: Microsoft instructs operators to generate rollback before importing a template to another computer.
findings.templateValidation: The validate command checks a security template file; it does not establish exact application or restore semantics for a single setting.

disposition.sourceReady: The documented command family is applicable to Windows 11 and Server 2025 and provides export, configure, rollback-generation and template-validation steps to evaluate on disposable systems.
unverified: Whether a one-setting PasswordComplexity template changes no unrelated account-policy field.
Whether generated rollback restores prior Enabled, Disabled and NotDefined local states exactly.
How local and merged exports represent managed precedence and absent values on each target.
disposition.nextAcceptance: On disposable Windows 11 and Server 2025 targets, validate the one-setting template, capture local and merged exports, apply and repeat, compare unrelated account-policy fields, generate/validate rollback, restore each prior state, and confirm no managed policy is misreported as a local effective value.

estimates.adjustment: None; official command semantics clarify the disposable-VM experiment but prove no lifecycle outcome.
